concept: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India
question: Who among the following was NOT associated with the ‘Prarthana Sabha’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Prarthana Samaj was a reform movement founded in 1867 in Bombay to make social and religious reforms in the Hindu society.
 
• Govind Ranade, RG Bhandarkar, and Atmaram Pandurang were prominent leaders associated with the Prarthana Samaj.
 
• The Samaj aimed at removing caste restrictions, encouraging widow remarriage, and promoting women's education.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi, although a prominent figure in Indian history, was not associated with the Prarthana Samaj.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Govind Ranade**

 
 
• Govind Ranade was a distinguished Indian scholar and social reformer.
 
• He played a significant role in the formation of the Indian National Congress.
 
• Ranade was also a judge of the Bombay High Court and an advocate for social reforms such as widow remarriage and the abolition of child marriage.
 
 
 
• **RG Bhandarkar**
 
 
• Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar was an Indian scholar, social reformer, and a prominent member of the Prarthana Samaj.
 
• He made significant contributions to the fields of Sanskrit and ancient Indian history.
 
• Bhandarkar was also involved in the establishment of the Bombay Anthropological Society.
 
 
 
• **Atmaram Pandurang**
 
 
• Atmaram Pandurang was the founder of the Prarthana Samaj.
 
• He was a physician and social reformer who worked towards the upliftment of the downtrodden sections of society.
 
• His efforts were directed towards promoting rational and progressive thinking in the Hindu community.
 
 
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**
 
 
• Mahatma Gandhi was a key figure in the Indian independence movement.
 
• He is known for his philosophy of non-violence (Ahimsa) and his role in leading India to independence from British rule.
 
• Gandhi was associated with various movements like the Non-Cooperation Movement, Civil Disobedience Movement, and the Quit India Movement.
